goal: Define the exact boundary between Apex-owned agent definitions and executor-native catalogs, then present an evidence-bounded strategy for whether agent.definition_catalog must remain REQUIRED.
scope: re-evaluation of agent.definition_catalog as a REQUIRED capability
Apex-owned definition projection contract for a generic executor
authority, identity, scheduling, verification, and semantic-success boundary analysis
Owner Decision Queue entry for any material architecture or authority change
out_of_scope: weakening AC-DEV-018 admission to force execution
changing the current REQUIRED capability or registry mappings without Owner approval
runtime dispatch while admission remains blocked
ECC installation, permanent executor selection, or executor-native integration
claiming generic executor injection is operationally proven without an adapter proof
architecture_constraints: Apex owns the canonical Agent/Skill Registry, task semantics, scheduling, authority, verification, and semantic success
an executor receives only a task-scoped immutable projection and cannot define or elevate Apex claims
agent.definition_catalog remains REQUIRED until an approved replacement contract and operational adapter evidence exist
architecture or authority boundary changes require Owner approval and must enter the Owner Decision Queue
NOT_PROVEN remains visible and no runtime work is dispatched while admission is blocked
acceptance_criteria: the exact native-catalog contract and the alternative Apex-owned-definition projection contract are written separately
the analysis identifies which identity, authority, scheduling, verification, and reconciliation facts remain Apex-owned
the strategy states whether generic executor invocation is safe only as a future adapter target or is operationally proven
current AC-DEV-017/018 REQUIRED semantics remain unchanged pending Owner decision
a material Owner Decision Queue item records the proposed boundary decision, affected contracts, evidence, and rollback posture
